831ef227aa959c0a: JELEBU: Negri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he was not informed of the sole menteri besar candidate submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

3b3206fe5f49c20d: SEREMBAN: A Chinese citizen who went viral for allegedly leaving his child near the Nilai toll plaza pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to exposing the 12-year-old to the risk of physical injury.
Jiao Bo, 45, entered the plea after the charge was read out in Mandarin by an interpreter before judge Datin M. Kunasundary.
According to the charge, Jiao, an engineer, had exposed the child in a manner likely to cause physical injury at 1.21pm at the Nilai toll plaza exit ramp.
The charge was framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, up to 20 years' imprisonment, or both, upon conviction.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Siti Khairiah Abdul Razak offered no bail, citing the seriousness of the offence and the fact that the accused is the victim's father.
Siti Khairiah also informed the court that the child is currently in the mother's care.
Counsel Shahmi Iffah Mohd Arshad requested minimum bail, arguing that Jiao is the family's sole breadwinner.
He said the accused has lived in Malaysia for 10 years on a company-sponsored employment pass with his wife and two children, aged 12 and eight.
"The accused manages all family affairs, including banking and the children's schooling.
"This is his first offence, either in Malaysia or China, and his detention has caused distress to his wife and emotional trauma to the children after seeing their father arrested by police," he said.
Shahmi Iffah added that Jiao was willing to live separately from the family home in Cheras to ensure there was no risk to the child's safety.
The court allowed bail of RM20,000 with two Malaysian sureties aged 21 and above, and ordered the accused to surrender his passport and refrain from approaching or disturbing the victim.
The court fixed Dec 17 for mention and submission of the forensic report.
It was previously reported that a man was arrested after leaving his child near the Nilai toll plaza on the North-South Expressway, following a viral video of the incident.

Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya had said that an argument between two siblings inside the car angered the father, prompting him to allegedly leave one of them behind as a lesson.

4f5f4d81e89f6af3: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's defamation suit against Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man will go to trial next year.
Anwar's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the five-day trial is scheduled for May 11 to 14 and May 28, with Dec 18 fixed for case management.

Anwar filed the suit against Tuan Ibrahim in August.
Sankara said the suit stems from allegedly false and defamatory statements made by Tuan Ibrahim during a political speech at Felda Jenderak Utara, Kuala Krau, Pahang, on or around June 14.

He said the suit also relates to the publication and republication of the allegedly defamatory statements in video recordings and on social media platforms, including YouTube and Facebook, as well as on the defendant's Facebook account, "@Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man."

Sankara said the reliefs sought include general, aggravated and exemplary damages, as well as an injunction barring Tuan Ibrahim from making, publishing, republishing or disseminating the statements or any with a similar meaning.

He said Anwar is also seeking an order for the removal of the posts from social media accounts and platforms under Tuan Ibrahim's custody or control, alongside interest, costs and other relief deemed just by the court.
Anwar had previously issued a letter of demand to Tuan Ibrahim over the matter.

40e0a45ce243679a: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 5.5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, surpassing the advance estimate of 5.3 per cent.
Bank Negara Malaysia said the stronger growth was driven by sustained household spending, increased investment activities and improved export performance, particularly in technology-related products.
On the domestic front, household spending was supported by favourable labour market conditions and steady income growth.
The central bank said export growth strengthened further, driven by technology-related shipments of both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products.

Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said Malaysia's E&E sector continued to benefit from strong global technology demand, supported by robust artificial intelligence-related investment.
"Reflecting this strength, domestic E&E exports accelerated to 66.9 per cent year-on-year growth in the third quarter.

"China, Singapore and the US remain Malaysia's top E&E export destinations, with exports to all three markets recording strong double-digit growth," he said at a joint press conference on Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 GDP performance.
Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.6 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, although third-quarter growth moderated from six per cent in the second quarter.
Rasheed said Malaysia's strong economic performance was expected to push full-year growth above five per cent in 2026.
He said the economy was well-positioned to sustain this momentum into 2027, supported by solid economic fundamentals and positive outcomes from ongoing structural reforms.
"Malaysia's economy is very likely to grow by up to five per cent in 2026 and between 4.2 per cent and 5.2 per cent in 2027, with domestic demand remaining a major driver of growth," he added.
Rasheed said the growth outlook remained subject to both upside and downside risks, including a further escalation of conflict in the Middle East and weaker-than-expected commodity production.

b83122cc79bbc245: NEW YORK: Anthropic prices its blockbuster IPO on Wednesday, giving ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant in a test of how long the artificial intelligence spending boom can last.
AI stocks have swung sharply as investors question whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.
Wall Street is also digesting the US midterm election results, which gave control of both chambers of Congress to Democrats, who are more wary of AI.

Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of the AI buildout and an early investor in Anthropic, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence reportedly believes could be a Chinese spy.
IPO windfall

Pricing is the step at which Anthropic and its underwriting banks set the final cost for shares sold to investors who placed orders in the offering, typically after markets close the evening before trading begins.
The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission last week that it plans to sell 825 million shares at US$70 to US$78 each.
Trading is expected to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," and the shares could quickly rise above the offering price. SpaceX shares jumped 19% on their first day of trading in June.

According to the filing, Anthropic's revenue has surged, reaching US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from US$1.4 billion a year earlier. Its annualised run-rate revenue was about US$81 billion as of Oct 31, up US$10 billion from the end of September.
At the top of the range, the offering would raise about US$64.4 billion, valuing the San Francisco-based company at about US$1.4 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares.
Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, now the company's chief executive and president, founded Anthropic with several colleagues five years ago after leaving ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.
Anthropic had been expected to raise up to US$100 billion, which would have been the largest IPO on record.
Instead, the offering will likely fall short of the US$86 billion that Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in June at a valuation of US$1.77 trillion.
Earlier estimates had put Anthropic's valuation as high as US$2 trillion, but such estimates fell as AI stocks slid on Wall Street.
Seven tech companies, including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft, have agreed to buy US$26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement.
The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.

According to an analysis by SaaStr, a software industry publication, Anthropic's more than 5,000 employees are set to bank more than US$200 billion in the IPO, a windfall that could ripple through the San Francisco economy.
In the filing, Anthropic's seven co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their personal equity in the company to charity.
Anthropic has also said it will put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund.
Together with the founders' pledge and an employee donation matching programme, that would dedicate roughly 20% of the company's shares to public purposes.
Anthropic's IPO filing gives extensive space to the risks of the technology, reflecting the company's focus on safety even as it builds ever more powerful models.
It warns that advanced AI systems "could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly".
It also says the company's public positions on AI regulation and safety could expose it to "political backlash, or disproportionate regulatory action".

The warning refers to Anthropic's feud with the Trump administration, which ordered federal agencies to stop using its technology and labeled it a supply-chain risk after the company refused to let the Pentagon use Claude for domestic mass surveillance or lethal autonomous weapons.

958447dcf77b5e42: WASHINGTON: Hakeem Jeffries is set to move closer Wednesday to becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives as Democrats prepare to choose their leader following a landslide midterm election victory.

The 56-year-old New Yorker faces no declared challenger in a closed-door party election, but opposition from some newly elected progressives has exposed divisions over how Democrats should use their newfound power.

Jeffries is poised to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump's term, with his party seeking to reverse the Republican president's policies and hold his administration to account.
He said Tuesday he would request a recorded vote on his nomination, departing from the wishes of some allies who had hoped he would be chosen "by acclamation" -- without a formal ballot.

Jeffries told reporters at the Capitol on the eve of the ballot that every Democrat should have the opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last won control of the House in 2018.
Wednesday's vote will select the party's nominee for speaker, but Jeffries must still win a formal election of the full House when the new Congress convenes on Jan 3.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers can participate in Wednesday's nomination, including progressives who have sought concessions from Jeffries on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.
Some have threatened to withhold their votes, although the dissent has not produced a rival candidate.
Jeffries and his allies have been working to consolidate support, meeting with newly elected lawmakers and reassuring different factions that their voices will be heard.
The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party's plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.
"Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one," he told reporters Tuesday.
"We're going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America."
Brooklyn roots
Raised in Brooklyn's Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artistes, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.
He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump's first impeachment trial in 2020.

His expected elevation would represent a landmark in American politics, putting him in charge of one of Washington's most powerful institutions and second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.
But Jeffries would inherit a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

The relatively straightforward House leadership election contrasts with a more competitive contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran leader Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.
Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.
Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate.

8bbe16ae8b0b44c3: KUALA LUMPUR: Sports public relations agency ShekhinahPR has received the International Business Excellence Award in recognition of its contributions to public relations, strategic communications and the media industry.
Former chief justice Zaki Azmi presented the award at the 2026 International CEO and Business Leaders Forum at Berjaya Times Square Hotel here yesterday.
ShekhinahPR founder and CEO Christopher Raj Aralanthu described the recognition as an achievement shared with employees, clients, strategic partners and media practitioners who supported the agency.
"We believe that effective communication, strong working relationships and commitment in everything we do are fundamental to the growth of any organisation.
"We are grateful for the continued trust and support of everyone who has been part of ShekhinahPR’s journey," he said in a statement.

Established in 2011, ShekhinahPR’s work includes public relations and media support for major football events, including the Maybank Challenge Cup 2025 between Manchester United and the Asean All-Stars, and the Chelsea-Johor Darul Ta’zim fixture.
The Chelsea-JDT match at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium on Aug 9 marked the Premier League club’s return to Malaysia after 13 years and its first appearance in Johor.

The agency’s involvement in football also extends to widening participation, having partnered with Portugal-based Integrated Dreams in September to help people with disabilities participate in the sport and pursue careers within the industry.
The partnership will focus on leadership development, education and inclusive football, with programmes planned in Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia from 2027.

The forum, jointly organised by KSI Strategic Institute for Asia Pacific, the World Business Chamber and other partners, brought together business leaders and industry experts to discuss how companies could adapt to economic and geopolitical uncertainty while strengthening resilience and growth.

Also honoured at the ceremony was FMT Media Sdn Bhd executive chairman Nelson Fernandez, who received the Global Captains of Industry Award, which recognises business leaders’ contributions to the Malaysian and global economy.
facf655d451013d4: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's balance of payments remains in surplus in the third quarter of 2026, with the current account recording a surplus of RM5.7 billion.
This was supported by stronger goods exports despite widening deficits in services and primary income, according to the Statistics Department.
It said the goods account surplus expanded to RM56.2 billion from RM40.7 billion in the preceding quarter, as exports rose to RM409.7 billion from RM359.3 billion.

Export growth was underpinned by stronger demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products, particularly those linked to artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, high-performance computing and advanced memory technologies, especially from the United States, Singapore and China.
However, the services account deficit widened sharply to RM6.9 billion from RM700 million in the second quarter.
Imports grew 17.9 per cent to RM97.3 billion, outpacing the 10.4 per cent increase in exports to RM90.4 billion.

The departmentvattributed the wider deficit mainly to other business services, which more than doubled to RM17 billion from RM8 billion, reflecting higher payments for professional and management consulting services, particularly in the E&E industry.
The primary income deficit also widened to RM41.8 billion from RM27.2 billion, driven by higher earnings of foreign companies operating in Malaysia, which reached RM64.3 billion during the quarter.
Meanwhile, the financial account reversed from a net outflow of RM27 billion in the preceding quarter to a net inflow of RM19.8 billion.
This was supported by stronger portfolio investment, other investment and direct investment flows.

Foreign direct investment (FDI) net inflows nearly doubled to RM14.3 billion from RM7.4 billion in the second quarter, reflecting improved business performance among foreign-owned companies, with higher profits retained for future expansion.
The services sector, particularly information and communication activities related to data centres, was the largest recipient of FDI, followed by manufacturing and mining and quarrying.
Singapore, Hong Kong and the United States were the leading sources of FDI during the quarter.
In contrast, direct investment abroad (DIA) recorded a slightly higher net outflow of RM7.6 billion against RM7 billion previously.
Investments were mainly channelled into mining and quarrying, followed by financial activities.
Saudi Arabia, the Netherlands and Thailand were the main destinations for Malaysian investments abroad.
On the international investment position, Malaysia's accumulated FDI position stood at RM1.23 trillion at end-September 2026, while its DIA position reached RM639.7 billion.
The country's total international financial assets amounted to RM2.89 trillion against liabilities of RM2.93 trillion, resulting in a net international investment liability position of RM36 billion.
International reserves stood at RM537.6 billion at the end of September.

b45b55644c6eb4d1: KOTA BARU: A Myanmar mother who returned to Malaysia illegally in search of work to support her family was arrested with two friends after crossing the border from Thailand into Kelantan.
Known only as Erika, the 30-year-old had been working as a cook at a restaurant in Puchong without valid documents since last year.
The mother of a toddler said she had paid a Thai agent RM3,000 to arrange her journey from Tak Bai, Thailand, to Selangor.
After returning to Myanmar last month, she decided to come back to Malaysia to resume her job, bringing two friends, aged 18 and 28, with her.
However, all three were arrested in Tumpat yesterday after entering the country illegally.
They were among nine undocumented migrants detained by police.
Erika said it was her first arrest.
"I know I have broken the law, but I have no other choice. I need to find work in Malaysia to support my family.
"I brought two close friends with me this time, but unfortunately, all three of us ended up facing the same fate," she said.
Myanmar has been gripped by conflict and economic hardship since the military seized power in a 2021 coup, prompting many people to seek work abroad, including in Malaysia.

8796587060816014: PETALING JAYA: The national unity ministry is continuing to strengthen the Rukun Negara as a shared basis for nation-building through various comprehensive measures to ensure that its principles are not only memorised but also understood, internalised and practised in daily life.
The ministry’s efforts have been expanded across all levels of society, from schools and higher education institutions to Parliament, the public service, communities and the corporate sector.
These strengthened efforts follow a Cabinet decision in 2023 for the Rukun Negara to be read fully, including its preface, in all official government programmes and school assemblies.

To strengthen the understanding of the Rukun Negara, national unity minister Aaron Ago Dagang launched Eksplorasi Rukun Negara, his inaugural initiative as a minister, providing pupils, university students and the public with opportunities to learn about, understand and appreciate its principles through direct experiences and interactions.

The initiative was then expanded to Parliament, with MPs reading the Rukun Negara at the beginning of each year’s session. Various state assemblies, including in Perak, also began doing the same from April 2025.

In the public service, efforts to cultivate patriotism and loyalty have been strengthened through General Circular No 1 of 2025, a directive for civil servants to recite the Rukun Negara at least once a week.

However, appreciation of the Rukun Negara does not stop at reciting it. The national unity ministry has also mobilised several programmes to incorporate the Rukun Negara into the public’s daily lives, including Gerak Integrasi Perpaduan, Rukun Negara Youth Tour, Jalinan Integrasi Mahasiswa, A Night at the National Museum, Arkib@Sekolah, Citra Negaraku, Debat Perpaduan, Dialog Perpaduan and Pidato Rukun Negara.

Rukun Negara modules have been implemented in Tabika Perpaduan kindergartens, while Rukun Negara clubs in schools and Rukun Negara secretariats at higher education institutions continue to be strengthened as platforms for shaping a generation that understands shared values, patriotism and national identity.
Aaron said the Rukun Negara remains relevant as Malaysia continues to face new challenges, including social polarisation, extremism, the spread of fake news, and changes in the digital landscape.
He said the principles introduced in 1970 continue to serve as a shared framework of values for Malaysia’s diverse communities.
“Five decades have passed, and the challenges faced by the world and our communities have changed. However, the need for shared values to guide our lives as Malaysians has never changed,” he said.

Aaron said the Rukun Negara should not be respected merely because it is a national symbol, but because its five principles form the basis for living together in a multiracial, multireligious and multicultural country.

“We may have different religions, cultures, languages and backgrounds, but we share one nation. The Rukun Negara provides shared values that bridge these differences and build a sense of belonging as Malaysians,” he said.
Aaron said the real question was not whether the Rukun Negara remains relevant after 50 years, but how deeply the people truly internalise and practise its principles in daily life.

“The Rukun Negara has not become outdated. What has changed are the times, technology and the challenges we face. As such, appreciation of the Rukun Negara must be kept alive in the context of each generation and current challenges,” he said.

Over five decades after the Rukun Negara was first declared, the government’s continuous efforts to promote appreciation of its principles show that its philosophy still has an important place in nation-building.

“The Rukun Negara is not merely meant to be memorised or recited. Its values must live in the people and be reflected in how we respect each other, the laws and national institutions and preserve harmony."

The national unity ministry emphasised that its agenda must move beyond merely reciting the Rukun Negara to appreciating and practising its five principles, so they are not merely treated as a text to be memorised but as values that shape the way Malaysians think, interact and carry out their duties as citizens.
e60f416b7b7a622e: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Perpaduan Negara (KPN) terus memperkukuh kedudukan Rukun Negara sebagai landasan bersama dalam pembinaan negara bangsa menerusi pelbagai langkah menyeluruh yang bukan sekadar memastikan ia dilafazkan tetapi turut difahami, dihayati dan diterjemahkan dalam kehidupan seharian rakyat.
Usaha itu diperluas merentasi pelbagai lapisan masyarakat, daripada peringkat sekolah dan institusi pendidikan tinggi (IPT) sehinggalah ke Parlimen, perkhidmatan awam, komuniti dan sektor korporat.

Langkah itu diperkukuh susulan persetujuan Jemaah Menteri pada 2023 supaya lafaz Rukun Negara dibaca secara penuh, bermula dengan mukadimah dan diikuti lima prinsip, dalam program rasmi kerajaan termasuk perhimpunan di sekolah.

Bagi memperkukuh kefahaman terhadap Rukun Negara, Menteri Perpaduan Negara, Aaron Ago Dagang, turut melancarkan Eksplorasi Rukun Negara sebagai inisiatif sulungnya, yang membuka ruang kepada murid sekolah, mahasiswa dan masyarakat awam untuk mengenali, memahami serta menghayati Rukun Negara melalui pengalaman dan interaksi secara lebih dekat.

Usaha itu kemudian diperluas ke Parlimen, dengan lafaz ikrar Rukun Negara oleh Ahli Parlimen pada pembukaan mesyuarat pertama setiap tahun. Di peringkat negeri, langkah sama turut dilaksanakan oleh beberapa DUN seperti di Perak bermula April 2025.

Dalam perkhidmatan awam pula, usaha membudayakan patriotisme dan taat setia turut diperkukuh menerusi Pekeliling Am Bilangan 1 Tahun 2025, yang memperuntukkan lafaz ikrar Rukun Negara oleh penjawat awam sekurang-kurangnya sekali seminggu.

Namun, penghayatan Rukun Negara tidak terhenti pada lafaz semata-mata. KPN turut menggerakkan pelbagai program bagi menjadikan Rukun Negara sebahagian daripada pengalaman hidup rakyat, antaranya Gerak Integrasi Perpaduan, Jelajah Belia Rukun Negara, Jalinan Integrasi Mahasiswa, Bermalam di Muzium, Arkib@Sekolah, Citra Negaraku, Debat Perpaduan, Dialog Perpaduan di IPT dan Pidato Rukun Negara.

Di peringkat pendidikan awal, modul Rukun Negara diterapkan di Tabika Perpaduan, manakala Kelab Rukun Negara di sekolah dan Sekretariat Rukun Negara di IPT terus diperkasa sebagai platform membentuk generasi yang memahami nilai bersama, patriotisme dan jati diri kebangsaan.
Menurut Aaron, Rukun Negara kekal relevan kerana Malaysia terus berdepan cabaran baharu termasuk polarisasi sosial, ekstremisme, penyebaran maklumat palsu dan perubahan landskap digital.
Katanya, prinsip yang diperkenalkan pada 1970 itu terus menjadi kerangka nilai bersama dalam mengurus kepelbagaian masyarakat Malaysia.

"Lima dekad telah berlalu, dunia berubah dan cabaran masyarakat turut berubah. Tetapi keperluan untuk mempunyai nilai bersama yang menjadi panduan kehidupan kita sebagai rakyat Malaysia tidak pernah berubah," katanya.

Beliau berkata, menghormati Rukun Negara bukan semata-mata kerana ia merupakan satu simbol kebangsaan, tetapi kerana lima prinsipnya membentuk asas kepada kehidupan bersama dalam sebuah negara yang berbilang kaum, agama dan budaya.

“Kita mungkin berbeza dari segi agama, budaya, bahasa dan latar belakang, tetapi kita berkongsi satu negara. Rukun Negara menyediakan nilai bersama yang mengikat perbezaan itu dan membina rasa kepunyaan sebagai rakyat Malaysia," katanya.
Aaron berkata, persoalan sebenar bukan sama ada Rukun Negara masih relevan selepas lebih 50 tahun, tetapi sejauh mana rakyat benar-benar menghayati dan mengamalkannya dalam kehidupan seharian.

“Rukun Negara tidak menjadi lapuk hanya kerana usianya. Yang berubah ialah zaman, teknologi dan cabaran kita. Sebab itu penghayatannya perlu terus dihidupkan dalam konteks generasi dan cabaran semasa," katanya.

Lebih lima dekad selepas Rukun Negara diisytiharkan, usaha berterusan kerajaan memperkukuh penghayatan prinsip itu menunjukkan bahawa falsafah berkenaan terus mempunyai tempat penting dalam pembinaan negara.

“Rukun Negara bukan sekadar untuk dihafal atau dilafaz. Ia mesti menjadi nilai yang hidup dalam diri rakyat bagaimana kita menghormati orang lain, menghormati undang-undang, menghormati institusi negara dan menjaga keharmonian bersama," katanya.

KPN menegaskan agenda itu perlu bergerak daripada sekadar lafaz kepada penghayatan dan seterusnya pengamalan, supaya lima prinsip Rukun Negara tidak hanya dikenali sebagai teks yang dihafal, tetapi menjadi nilai yang membentuk cara rakyat Malaysia berfikir, berinteraksi dan melaksanakan tanggungjawab sebagai warganegara.

96a15e0cb4478253: SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told global and business leaders today there was a need for genuine multilateralism, equitable technology sharing and human-centric development.

Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Centre, the prime minister said global leaders and the business community must ensure economic progress does not marginalise emerging economies.
Stressing the need for a fairer global economic architecture, he said true international cooperation cannot be one-sided.
"We must respect multilateral arrangements. You cannot, with one voice, claim to promote trade and investment, but restrict it only to your own country," he said.
"The entire multilateral framework must change; we have entered into a new era of assertiveness. Small and emerging countries must be treated with respect and dignity."
Earlier, Chinese President Xi Jinping opened the summit with a pledge to open China's market to more global products and services while upholding multilateralism and the rule of law.

In his opening speech, Xi said China would not only cut tariffs and expand market access for global producers, but also reform rules, regulations and standards to ease entry into its 1.4 billion-strong market.
Positioning Malaysia as a key trading nation expanding investments from both the United States and China, Anwar commended Beijing's leadership for opening its markets to the world.

He said the current geopolitical climate requires advanced nations to go beyond offering market access, urging them to share their experiences and technological breakthroughs — particularly in sectors such as semiconductors and artificial intelligence — with developing nations.
Anwar reminded corporate leaders that emerging economies, many of which endured decades of colonialism and oppression, need these investments to revitalise their economies.

Reiterating the importance of Asean centrality, he said powerful countries cannot impose their circumstances on smaller nations, adding that trade and investment must uplift broader societies rather than serve isolated geopolitical interests.
Turning to the corporate sector, Anwar underscored the business community's vital role in shaping the Asia-Pacific region's future.

He challenged CEOs to look beyond immediate commercial success and immediate profit margins, reminding them that the partnerships they forge and the technologies they develop carry a profound social responsibility.
The ultimate goal of corporate investment, he noted, should be to strengthen domestic economies and develop human capital so that emerging economies can move up the value chain.

"The true measure of economic progress must ultimately be found in the lives it transforms," Anwar concluded, setting forth a vision for the Asia-Pacific where nations retain the freedom to chart their own destinies.

Achieving this, he warned, will require immense political courage and a rejection of growth models that lead to further inequity and neglect, ensuring that the wealth and wisdom of the region are shared by all.

The Apec CEO Summit 2026 is part of the Apec Economic Leaders' Week taking place in Shenzhen from Nov 12 to 20, drawing more than 2,000 business and political representatives from 21 Apec and 13 non-Apec economies.

0e12b5198c762bf5: PETALING JAYA: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has slammed the Penang government over the state water company's agreement to pay Perak RM210 million annually for 40 years, even if no treated water is supplied to Penang.
Lim accused Penang chief minister Chow Kon Yeow and state executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari of failing to explain the rationale behind this condition.
The Bagan MP said the arrangement was exposed by five independent directors of PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAH) during an extraordinary general meeting on Nov 12.
The five dissenting directors were Brian Tan, Lim Eng Huat, Nor Hatina Salleh, Lim Seang Lee and Raja Azmi Raja Nazuddin.
Lim said they objected to the Penang Water Supply Corporation's (PBAPP) proposed purchase of treated water from Perak under the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme.

"Chow and Zairil have disappointed the people of Penang by refusing to explain why PBAPP must still pay RM210 million annually for 40 years, or a total of RM8.4 billion, to Perak even if not a single drop of treated water is supplied to Penang.

"The five directors were concerned that PBAPP would remain liable for the annual capacity charges even if it received less than the contracted 300 million litres of treated water or, in the worst-case scenario, none at all," he said in a statement.
Lim said the agreement, which is scheduled to take effect on March 31, 2032, would commit PBAPP to paying Perak at least RM24.6 billion over 40 years.
This comprises RM8.4 billion in fixed capacity charges and RM16.2 billion in supply charges.
He said the supply charges could increase as the initial tariff of RM1.70 per cubic metre was subject to upward revisions over the 40-year period, eventually reaching RM7.21 per cubic metre.
"The tariff charged to consumers could rise by another RM1 per cubic metre to account for other costs incurred by PBAPP."
Lim said the tariff could exceed RM7.21 per cubic metre following a contractual review after 22 years.

While questioning the price of treated water purchased from Perak, Lim said the more pressing concern was the mandatory capacity payment, which PBAPP would have to make regardless of whether it received any water.
He described the arrangement as unequal and potentially undermining public confidence in the state government's handling of the agreement.
173aa77f9674d2e3: PETALING JAYA: Adun Pantai Jerejak Fahmi Zainol mempersoalkan pendirian DAP Pulau Pinang yang masih mengekalkan Umno dalam pentadbiran negeri, ketika hubungan antara Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan Barisan Nasional (BN) semakin tegang.

“Sampai bila DAP Pulau Pinang nak kekalkan Umno dalam pentadbiran kerajaan negeri Pulau Pinang setelah bergaduh di Johor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka dan semalam berbalas pantun disindir tapi masih mengekalkan Umno di Pulau Pinang,” katanya menerusi TikTok.
“Sesal dahulu pendapatan, sesal kemudian hilang Komtar,” tambah wakil rakyat PKR itu, memberi amaran secara berkias mengenai kesan politik jika keadaan berkenaan berterusan.

Fahmi menjadi wakil rakyat PKR pertama secara terbuka mempersoalkan kedudukan Umno dalam kerajaan Pulau Pinang selepas penasihat DAP Lim Guan Eng mencabar Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi pada September lalu supaya turut mendesak PH menyingkirkan partinya daripada pentadbiran negeri.

Bagaimanapun, Ketua Menteri Chow Kon Yeow yang juga pengerusi PH Pulau Pinang menolak gesaan Guan Eng, dengan menjelaskan pandangan itu bukan pendirian parti dan sebarang keputusan perlu menunggu ketetapan Majlis Presiden PH.

Pada Ogos lalu, kepimpinan PH Pulau Pinang sebulat suara memutuskan untuk meneruskan kerjasama dengan BN dan mengekalkan Adun Sungai Acheh Rashidi Zinol sebagai exco, meskipun BN menjalin kerjasama dengan Perikatan Nasional (PN) di Negeri Sembilan.

Hubungan kedua-dua gabungan itu semakin renggang selepas persaingan pada PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan, sebelum kerjasama BN-PN meraih kemenangan besar di Melaka Sabtu lalu dengan menguasai 24 daripada 28 kerusi DUN. PH hanya memenangi empat kerusi, semuanya menerusi DAP.

Ketegangan itu turut merebak ke Dewan Rakyat apabila Timbalan Menteri Kerja Raya Ahmad Maslan menyampaikan pantun yang didakwa menyindir PH pada Isnin, sekali gus mencetuskan bantahan beberapa Ahli Parlimen gabungan itu, termasuk RSN Rayer (Jelutong).

Sebelum ini, Timbalan Pengerusi PH Pulau Pinang Faiz Fadzil turut menggesa kedudukan Umno dalam kerajaan negeri dibincangkan susulan serangan pemimpin parti itu terhadap PH. Mesyuarat yang dijadualkan pada September bagaimanapun ditangguhkan ke bulan ini.
cf104d200d66f9bd: PETALING JAYA: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reportedly ordered Ismail Lasim to continue performing his duties as menteri besar as usual.
This follows an audience granted to the Juasseh assemblyman yesterday evening, which lasted over an hour.
During the meeting, Tuanku Muhriz instructed Ismail to continue serving as menteri besar, Harian Metro reported.

It is unclear if the ruler rejected his supposed resignation or needs time to verify or deliberate on the matter. However, Ismail has continued attending events and meetings as menteri besar, based on his social media posts.
Barisan Nasional (BN) announced Ismail’s resignation as menteri besar on Monday, while coalition chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said it had submitted the name of a candidate to succeed Ismail.
However, the palace said yesterday that it had yet to verify Ismail’s resignation as the supposed letter was only sent to Istana Hinggap at 12.16am on Tuesday by an individual from a law firm.
It said according to the state’s constitution, the menteri besar must submit his resignation to the Yang Dipertuan Besar, and that it will only take effect with the ruler’s consent.
This led to questions over BN purportedly preceding the palace in announcing Ismail's supposed resignation.

Ismail's son Naim also questioned the matter, saying his father did not issue a statement on his resignation, and warned against making the menteri besar a scapegoat for the vested interest of a select few.
597c8555152a742c: SHENZHEN: Chinese president Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.

Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US president Donald Trump on Thursday.

"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.

"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region," he said.
Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".
He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
"Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Trade tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit has approached.
Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.
On the sidelines of last year's Apec summit in South Korea, Trump and Xi reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.
The US this week announced tougher restrictions on the export to China of advanced semiconductors used to train and run AI models, controls it says are needed for national security.

The new US rules crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries full of chips designed by the Californian giant Nvidia.

Nvidia on Wednesday reported blockbuster earnings but the results were overshadowed by a widening scandal sparked by former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman suspected by US officials of spying for China.

18d429f57b356b9d: SINGAPORE: Singapore is setting out three artificial intelligence missions spanning financial crime, business lending and AI-agent transactions as it expands the technology’s use in finance, deputy prime minister Gan Kim Yong said.

Five banks are already pooling transaction data so AI can spot scam patterns that individual lenders may miss, while the Monetary Authority of Singapore plans a study early next year for a shared detection system, Gan said in his keynote address at the Singapore FinTech Festival on Wednesday.
“Scams are not confined within the boundary of one bank,” Gan, who also chairs the MAS, said. “A victim’s money can pass through several institutions within minutes.”

The finance industry, which accounts for about 14% of Singapore’s economy and employs roughly 200,000 people, is becoming a test case for how far AI can be built into a major financial centre without undermining jobs, operations or trust. The push comes as some US banks block outside AI agents from moving customers’ money over concerns about security, control and who is responsible when something goes wrong.

Gan also addressed new US rules on remote access to advanced chips, which require licenses to export them to five countries, including Singapore. The government is working with affected companies to assess the impact and engaging US authorities on how to maintain access, he said.

“We value our international reputation, and we do not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities,” Gan said. “We will act against those who flout our laws.”

The latest initiatives are part of National AI Missions announced by prime minister Lawrence Wong in February, with financial services among four areas targeted for wider use of the technology. Twenty-three banks, insurers and asset managers have pledged to train more than 80,000 Singapore employees in AI skills by 2028 as firms study how jobs and tasks will change.

For financial crime, MAS plans to use lessons from the five-bank trial to design a shared system that can identify suspicious activity across institutions. The first phase will focus on Singapore, though Gan said there may eventually be opportunities to work with other jurisdictions as scams cross borders.

The financing mission, meanwhile, will test whether more data can help lenders assess smaller companies and startups that may lack long credit histories or assets to use as security. AI could eventually identify when a viable business needs funding and alert it to suitable options before it applies.
Singapore will also test AI agents that can make payments or purchases on behalf of people and companies, potentially speeding up transactions and enabling new forms of machine-led commerce.

“However, greater autonomy must come with clear responsibility and accountability,” Gan said. The systems would operate within defined limits, with firms remaining accountable for actions taken on their behalf.
119423f18f2d312f: KUALA LUMPUR: An opposition member of parliament (MP) has asked whether the government had assessed the combined impact of a planned 1,623-acre industrial development in Bukit Kerayong, Kapar, on flooding, water supply, electricity and infrastructure.

2bd6c873d1821f4d: SHENZHEN: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin were set to meet on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

Thursday's trilateral summit has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.
Washington had signalled that Ukraine was not expected to be addressed — something Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — before Trump said it would be.

China has said only that the leaders would hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations" on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting.
Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.
In from the cold
Putin, who arrived in Shenzhen early on Wednesday, has been shunned by the West since launching Europe's worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine.
Xi and Putin were both due to address the Apec gathering before discussing energy and finance and then, in a smaller format, foreign policy, including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said.
Xi on Wednesday called for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade.
"Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Kim incoming?
Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he had met fellow Quad leaders Australia, Japan and India a day earlier.
He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and possibly North Korea's Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen.
He added that Kim "would like" to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming a meeting with Kim.
"If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio said in Manila.
Trump's Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit was the security alliance's first since his return to power in January 2025.
The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence.
Trump's visit to the Philippines saw protests by around 2,000 people carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica" — a reference to a US supply chain initiative.
Tariffs, chips and rare earths
While Asean leaders grappled with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump's ongoing tariff blitz loomed large.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a "countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism" while touting Beijing's expanding trade with the bloc.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada's Mark Carney struck a similar note on trade, with both explicitly citing the need to reduce their dependence on the US market.
On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch up with China in rare earths production "within 10 months".
Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle Asean members.
Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion".
Singapore responded by saying it was exploring ways to facilitate "trusted access" for firms based in the city-state.
Pax Silica
Trump was set to meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen.
Aimed at countering China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines as it threatens to displace Indigenous families.

"We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people," Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday's protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words "Pax Silica Sashay Away!"

40d315f6b6f1cd5d: TEHRAN: Kuwait said on Wednesday it was countering "hostile drone attacks", as Washington's Gulf allies remained on alert hours after the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early Wednesday, a day after Tehran's Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base in the country used by Washington.

The interceptions come as the US and Iran remain in a standoff over the key waterway, a conduit for global energy shipments, despite a lull in the war triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
The conflict has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities, as Tehran stepped up retaliatory attacks.
Kuwait's military said Wednesday its air defences were "responding to hostile drone threats", urging its public to follow security and safety advice.
Earlier, Iran's official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the US had hit Qeshm Island without causing serious damage.

US fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island", an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets".
Washington and Tehran have vied for control over the Hormuz strait, with the US military working to protect ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Iran's attempts to close it.
Despite Washington and Tehran holding back from a full resumption of hostilities, tensions remain high.
On Tuesday, US President Donald Trump said he was taking "very seriously" reports that Iran was developing plans to use a so-called "dirty bomb" in Washington.

CNN cited seven anonymous US officials as saying Iran was plotting how to target senior administration figures with a bomb laced with chemical or radioactive material, though they stopped short of saying Iran planned to carry out such an attack.

"If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before," Trump said, adding: "I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the report and called it "Iraq War-style propaganda".
Earlier on Tuesday, explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.
The attack was in response to the "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones", it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, but had not been hit for weeks until Iranian drone attacks on Friday and Sunday.

5a45f9239fdc5868: MONTREAL: The new separatist government in Canada's Quebec province is backing legislation to ban schoolchildren from wearing religious symbols in classrooms, a controversial proposal condemned by a key civil liberties group on Tuesday.

Secularism is a core issue in Quebec, a majority French-speaking province where the Catholic Church held huge influence over public institutions until the so-called Quiet Revolution of the 1960s led to broad reforms and a diminished church role.
Quebec's previous government, known by its French acronym CAQ, which was defeated in provincial elections last month, worked to further entrench secularism in the public sector.
It passed legislation banning public-sector employees, including teachers, from wearing religious symbols - such as a hijab, cross or kippah - at work.
Backlash against the law sparked a legal challenge involving civil society groups, the National Council of Canadian Muslims and others.
Canada's Supreme Court is set to issue its ruling on the case in the coming weeks.

The new minority government elected last month, headed by the separatist Parti Quebecois (PQ), said in a statement that it is "committed to maintaining the gains" of the previous government but wants to add new measures.
Those include "a ban, for all elementary school students, from wearing conspicuous religious clothing and symbols whose use leads to being immediately identified by one's religious affiliation".

Separatist Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has said his party "made a commitment ... to act resolutely in favor of secularism," arguing that keeping religion out of public schools would "protect the freedom of conscience of all Quebec students".
The Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA) on Tuesday called the PQ's proposal "deeply troubling."

"Children's access to education should never be conditional on whether the government approves of their religious identity or expression," CCLA equality director Harini Sivalingam said in a statement.
The leader of the opposition Liberals last week accused the PQ of "playing politics on the backs of children".
The PQ cannot pass legislation without opposition support.
Quebec's new legislative session opens on Dec 1, and so far only the opposition Conservatives have indicated an openness to the new measures.
ae1c45ea52dd0599: PETALING JAYA: Bekas menteri besar Selangor, Khir Toyo, meninggalkan Bersatu untuk menyertai Wawasan, lebih setahun selepas menyertai parti yang dipimpin bekas perdana menteri Muhyiddin Yassin itu.
Bekas Adun Sungai Panjang selama tiga penggal itu memberitahu FMT bahawa beliau menyertai Wawasan pimpinan Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin hampir sebulan lalu.

1d2e8f26fb4481f8: PETALING JAYA: Former Selangor menteri besar Khir Toyo has left Bersatu to join Wawasan, just over a year after joining the party led by ex-prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin.
The former three-term Sungai Panjang assemblyman told FMT that he joined opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin's Wawasan almost a month ago.
"I left Bersatu because the party seems to have lost its purpose and is constantly fighting among itself," he said.
A source from Wawasan earlier told FMT that Khir joined the party following the Negeri Sembilan election on Aug 1.
A Bersatu source also confirmed Khir’s departure, saying he joined the party to pursue an opportunity to run in elections.
"He joined for a short period just to contest, and then left again because he wanted to contest," the source said.
Khir's entry into Bersatu was made public in August last year by then Melaka Bersatu chief Abdul Rahim Thamby Chik, who is now also in Wawasan.
Khir and Rahim were both formerly from Umno.

Khir served as Selangor menteri besar from 2000 to 2008. He was jailed for a year in 2015 after being convicted of abusing his power in connection with the purchase of two plots of land and a house in Shah Alam. He was released on parole after serving six months.
Khir sought to revive his political career ahead of the 15th general election in 2022, declaring his intention to contest the Sungai Besar parliamentary seat.
However, Barisan Nasional opted to field then Sungai Besar Umno chief Jamal Yunos, who lost the seat to a Perikatan Nasional candidate.
d7ac552c1e5fbe9b: MANILA: US president Donald Trump is "serious" about seeking dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Wednesday, amid speculation about a possible meeting between the two during Trump's ongoing Asia trip, Yonhap News Agency reported.
Rubio made the remarks to the travelling White House press pool in Manila when asked whether Trump's idea of meeting Kim was a serious proposal or merely a possibility being floated.
"It's serious in the sense that I think the president has never viewed meeting and talking to someone as a concession," Rubio said.

The secretary added that Trump believes dialogue is necessary to resolve disputes with countries with which the United States has disagreements, reiterating that meeting a foreign leader does not mean endorsing that leader's actions.
"If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we are ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," he said.
Rubio, however, acknowledged that a meeting "may not happen," while saying Trump was "prepared to do it."
"Whether that will lead to a positive outcome, we will never find out if we don't try," Rubio said.

Trump and Kim held three in-person meetings during Trump's first term, beginning with their historic summit in Singapore in June 2018, followed by a second meeting in Hanoi in February 2019 and a brief encounter at the inter-Korean border village of Panmunjom in June that year.
The meetings, however, failed to produce any tangible progress towards denuclearisation or a lasting agreement regarding the Korean Peninsula.

Trump has repeatedly expressed interest in meeting Kim again. Before departing for Asia on Monday, he told reporters that he might meet Kim in China, adding that Kim's possible visit would be up to Chinese president Xi Jinping.

Rubio is accompanying Trump on his Asia trip, which began with his arrival in Manila on Tuesday. Trump attended a meeting of the Quad grouping of the US, Japan, Australia and India, as well as a special summit with Asean leaders, before heading to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders' meeting.
Trump later said Kim "would like to" attend the Apec summit in Shenzhen, further fuelling speculation about a possible meeting between the two leaders. But no meeting has been confirmed so far.

2d6aaa00f1571d75: PETALING JAYA: Bekas ketua menteri Pulau Pinang Lim Guan Eng membidas penggantinya Chow Kon Yeow dan exco Zairil Khir Johari berhubung kewajipan Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP) membayar caj kapasiti RM210 juta setahun kepada Perak.
Beliau yang juga Ahli Parlimen Bagan mempersoalkan mengapa bayaran berjumlah RM8.4 bilion sepanjang 40 tahun tetap perlu dibuat walaupun PBAPP berisiko tidak menerima sebarang bekalan air terawat.

Menurutnya, isu terbabit dibangkitkan lima daripada 12 pengarah PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAH), syarikat induk PBAPP, yang secara rasmi membantah perjanjian pembelian air terawat bernilai RM24.6 bilion pada mesyuarat agung luar biasa (EGM), 12 Nov lalu.

Beliau mendakwa lima pengarah bebas itu bimbang PBAPP tetap diwajibkan membayar caj kapasiti RM210 juta setahun walaupun menerima bekalan kurang daripada kuantiti minimum 300 juta liter sehari yang dipersetujui atau langsung tidak menerima sebarang bekalan.
"Chow Kon Yeow dan Zairil Khir Johari telah mengecewakan rakyat Pulau Pinang," katanya dalam kenyataan.

Mengikut perjanjian di bawah Skim Bekalan Air Perak Utara, PBAPP dijangka menanggung komitmen RM24.6 bilion selama 40 tahun bermula 31 Mac 2032, merangkumi caj kapasiti tetap RM8.4 bilion dan caj bekalan air terawat RM16.2 bilion.

Lim turut mempersoalkan kadar tarif asas air terawat yang bermula pada RM1.70 setiap meter padu, yang menurutnya boleh meningkat kepada RM7.21 sepanjang tempoh perjanjian, malah berpotensi menjadi lebih tinggi selepas semakan kontrak pada tahun ke-22.
Katanya, kos tambahan yang ditanggung PBAPP juga boleh menyebabkan tarif kepada pengguna meningkat sehingga RM1 lagi bagi setiap meter padu.
Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan isu utama bukan semata-mata harga air, sebaliknya kewajipan membayar caj kapasiti walaupun tiada bekalan diterima.

"Sekurang-kurangnya kita membayar untuk sesuatu yang diterima, iaitu air terawat," katanya, sambil menyifatkan perjanjian itu tidak adil, tidak rasional dan bercanggah dengan prinsip tadbir urus baik serta kepimpinan bertanggungjawab.

Sebelum ini, Chow berkata Pulau Pinang boleh menarik diri daripada perjanjian itu tanpa membayar pampasan sekiranya caj yang dipersetujui tidak mendapat kelulusan Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Air Negara (SPAN).
Pembekal air Perak diberi tempoh sehingga 2035 untuk memperoleh kelulusan berkenaan.
Bagaimanapun, 97.9% undi pemegang saham pada EGM 12 Nov menyokong perjanjian itu.

Skim berkenaan dirancang membekalkan antara 300 juta hingga 500 juta liter air terawat sehari kepada Pulau Pinang bagi memperkukuh jaminan bekalan negeri yang kini memperoleh kira-kira 80% air mentahnya dari Sungai Muda.

c0ad7286d1f6fd4e: SHENZHEN: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.

Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday.

"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.
"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region."
Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".
He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
"Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Trade tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit approaches.
Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.
On the sidelines of last year's APEC summit in South Korea, Trump and Xi reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.
The United States this week announced tougher restrictions on the export to China of advanced semiconductors used to train and run AI models, controls it says are needed for national security.

The new US rules crack down not only on chip smuggling but also on the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries full of chips designed by the Californian giant Nvidia.

Nvidia on Wednesday reported blockbuster earnings but the results were overshadowed by a widening scandal sparked by former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman suspected by US officials of spying for China.
d166a86f5c08393c: BEIJING: Xi Jinping urged Asia-Pacific economies to deepen cooperation as he warned against rising unilateralism and protectionism, setting out a defence of free trade as China hosts global leaders for high-stakes talks on trade and technology.

“Global growth lacks momentum, and unilateralism and protectionism are rampant,” the Chinese president told the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday. He called for closer technology partnerships and efforts to keep global supply chains stable and open.

“China has stood up unilateralism and protectionism and remained committed to true multilateralism,” Xi said, vowing to cut tariffs, expand market access and foster a more stable environment for foreign investments.

China will play host to a week of diplomacy and dealmaking as the Apec event get underway. Xi has already wrapped up several bilateral meetings, including talks with Canadian prime minister Mark Carney during which both countries agreed to further tariff relief on agricultural and steel exports.

Xi is also expected to meet with his US counterpart, Donald Trump, and Russian president Vladimir Putin, before sitting down with them together for unprecedented talks between the leaders of the world’s three biggest nuclear powers.

The Xi-Trump summit coincides with an escalating US push to restrict China’s access to the computing power needed to develop advanced AI. New US rules released this week target Chinese companies’ use of overseas data centers and access to chips through third countries, drawing a threat of retaliation from Beijing just days before Xi meets Trump to shore up their fragile trade truce.

In addition to Xi, the leaders of 11 other Apec economies - including Australia, Chile, Indonesia, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico and Vietnam - are also attending the CEO Summit that runs Nov 17-18, state media Xinhua News Agency reported.

Even as Xi showcases China’s tech prowess in Shenzhen, the world’s second-biggest economy is flashing numerous warning signs. Official figures released on Monday showed a slowdown across the board, underscoring the sluggish domestic demand that’s prompted complaints from China’s major trading partners.
7e3a0418a3f30ec6: SAN FRANCISCO: US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.

Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor – interim CEO Colette Kress – said that it was now "business as usual" at the company as it charts a way ahead without him.
Harvey Jones, the chair of the company's board, said in an earnings call that "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.
"Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.
She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent.
Huang's bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia – which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke – and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.
- Battle over AI chips -
"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said, hours before the earnings release.
"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil – countries the US Commerce Department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.
While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang's affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed – a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.
Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang's aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.
Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life."

e7c595b2c07eaf99: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian songstress Ernie Zakri enjoyed a rare career highlight yesterday after sharing the stage with French President Emmanuel Macron for a duet of the classic "La Vie En Rose".

48b59089ddf0f13c: PETALING JAYA: Two illegal workers at a fishing farm in Pontian, Johor, were each sentenced to 11 years in prison by the Johor Bahru High Court today for smuggling three fellow countrymen into Malaysia.

Judicial Commissioner Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor handed down the jail sentences to Indonesians Najril Ilham and Iswadi Ibrahim after they pleaded guilty to charges under Section 26A of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act.
The court ordered for their sentences to run from April 2, the date of their arrest.
Najril and Iswadi were charged with smuggling three other Indonesians on April 1 at a floating fish cage platform in Kukup.
According to case facts, Pontian police raided the area and found an Indonesian man acting as a "caretaker" of the floating house unit.
They also found three other Indonesians in the unit who were attempting to flee Malaysia. All of them failed to produce valid identification for the police.
Najril and Iswadi then arrived in boats to pick up the three Indonesians. Police seized their boats but both men fled the scene.
Police arrested them the next day in a shop at Kukup.
In meting out the sentence, Fareed said the court placed public interest as the main consideration in imposing the 11-year sentence.
"The court takes into account that their offences are extremely serious as this could expose Malaysia to a real security threat.
"The court takes a serious view of foreign nationals entering Malaysia, whether legally or illegally, and committing serious crimes without the slightest fear of the law.
"This cannot be tolerated. If enforcement is not carried out stringently, it will pave the way for more serious offences such as armed territorial incursion," said the judge.
d662e5a418d5a8d0: PETALING JAYA: Cabaran undang-undang 10 bekas anggota Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (Exco) Negeri Sembilan berhubung pembatalan pelantikan mereka berakhir secara mengejut selepas mereka menarik balik saman susulan peletakan jawatan Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim.
Bagaimanapun, penarikan balik itu melibatkan kos apabila Mahkamah Tinggi Seremban memerintahkan 10 Adun berkenaan membayar RM48,000 kepada responden.

Hakim Ros Mawar Rozain membatalkan saman itu tanpa kebenaran untuk memfailkannya semula dan memerintahkan plaintif membayar RM20,000 setiap seorang kepada Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri, Zafir Ibrahim, dan kerajaan Negeri Sembilan, serta RM8,000 lagi kepada Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU).
"Litigan berhak menarik balik tindakan undang-undang mereka dan kami tidak akan menghalang perkara itu," katanya ketika prosiding secara dalam talian.
Hakim juga menyuarakan kebimbangan terhadap sumber mahkamah yang telah digunakan untuk mendengar pelbagai permohonan segera sejak beberapa bulan lalu.

Pada awal prosiding hari ini, peguam Hafarizam Harun, yang mewakili bekas anggota Exco itu, memaklumkan kepada mahkamah bahawa beliau menerima arahan daripada anak guamnya untuk menarik balik saman berkenaan kerana perkembangan semasa menyebabkan saman itu tidak lagi relevan.
"Merujuk kepada duluan kes, apabila menteri besar meletakkan jawatan, anggota Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri beliau juga perlu berundur," katanya.
Hakim mencelah dengan menyatakan bahawa laporan menunjukkan Ismail belum meletakkan jawatan dan beliau juga bukan pihak dalam prosiding itu.
Hafarizam menjawab bahawa anak guamnya masih menunggu titah Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir berhubung peletakan jawatan Ismail itu.
Beliau turut memohon maaf kepada hakim kerana hanya memaklumkan penarikan balik saman itu pagi ini, selepas menulis surat kepada mahkamah semalam untuk memohon penangguhan lanjut.
Beliau berkata perkara itu telah dibincangkan dengan peguam pihak responden dan beliau memberi aku janji bahawa tiada permohonan baharu akan difailkan.

Pada Isnin, Ros Mawar membenarkan 10 Adun itu — lapan daripada Barisan Nasional (BN) dan dua daripada Perikatan Nasional — mendapatkan penangguhan sehingga hari ini bagi memberi mereka masa meneroka kemungkinan penyelesaian secara baik dengan pihak responden.
Menurut BN, Ismail meletakkan jawatan sebagai menteri besar pada Isnin.
Peguam Cyrus Das, yang mewakili setiausaha kerajaan negeri, menegaskan bahawa tiada lagi saman boleh difailkan susulan penarikan balik itu, termasuk permohonan untuk semakan kehakiman.
Sepuluh bekas exco itu memfailkan saman pemula di Mahkamah Tinggi Seremban pada 5 Okt lalu dengan menamakan setiausaha kerajaan negeri dan kerajaan negeri sebagai responden.
DKU ditambah sebagai responden ketiga, selepas permohonannya untuk mencelah dibenarkan.
Pihak responden berhasrat mencabar kesahihan saman pemula itu dengan berhujah 10 bekas exco terbabit sepatutnya mengambil tindakan undang-undang melalui semakan kehakiman.

Semua bekas exco itu memohon deklarasi mahkamah bahawa warta kerajaan negeri yang membatalkan pelantikan mereka tidak sah dan terbatal. Mereka turut menuntut ganti rugi, termasuk ganti rugi teladan dan teruk.

Mereka kehilangan jawatan selepas Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan mereka susulan dakwaan penyingkiran baginda April lalu adalah sah dan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar menjadi pemerintah baharu.
Pihak istana mendapati tindakan mereka memungkiri sumpah taat setia kepada pemerintah dan institusi diraja.
Abdul Rashid Ismail dan empat lagi peguam mewakili setiausaha kerajaan negeri, manakala Razlan Hadri Zulkifli dan Marisa Regina Aris Rizal mewakili kerajaan negeri.
Steven Thiru, Shafrin Halim dan dua lagi peguam mewakili DKU.
5bbd51f75c003242: I AM deeply saddened by the tragic accident involving a police van near Tapah on the North-South Expressway, which claimed the life of 26-year-old Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob and left 10 other police personnel injured.
My heartfelt condolences go to the family of the deceased. I also wish the injured personnel a speedy and full recovery.

This tragedy is a painful reminder that road safety must extend to everyone, including those who serve and protect the public. Police personnel travelling on official duties must be assured that the vehicles they use are safe, roadworthy and properly maintained.
While preliminary investigations suggest that a sudden burst of the van's rear tyre may have caused the accident, the incident raises several important questions that deserve serious attention.

First, there must be a comprehensive review of the maintenance and inspection procedures for police vehicles, particularly those used for long-distance journeys. Tyres, braking systems, steering mechanisms and other critical components must be inspected regularly and systematically.

Second, the safety of police personnel travelling in official vehicles must be given priority. Proper seating arrangements, functioning seat belts and compliance with vehicle passenger capacity are essential safeguards.

Third, there should be a thorough investigation into the accident to establish all contributing factors, beyond the preliminary finding of a burst tyre. The findings should be used to identify weaknesses and prevent similar tragedies.

I also believe that occupational safety and health principles must be given greater emphasis within enforcement agencies. Police personnel are exposed to occupational risks not only when confronting criminals or performing enforcement duties but also when travelling in vehicles as part of their work.
Their safety must therefore be recognised as an important component of workplace safety and health management.

The tragedy should prompt police and other enforcement agencies to undertake a comprehensive safety audit of their vehicle fleets and strengthen preventive maintenance and operational safety procedures.
We must not wait for another life to be lost before taking corrective action.
Every life matters, including the lives of those who dedicate themselves to protecting our communities. Their safety must never be taken for granted.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE SAFETY ADVOCATE
d9412423af1bccea: PADANG BESAR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) in Perlis has detected illegal e-hailing services operated by female drivers exclusively for passengers of the same gender.
Its director, Noraini Mohd Nawi, said the services were being widely promoted on social media platforms such as Telegram and Threads.
She said two cases involving female drivers were detected and action taken during monitoring and enforcement operations between January and October.
During the same period, the department issued 31 notices for various offences related to illegal passenger transport services and seized 14 vehicles.
The offences involved misuse of a Motor Vehicle Licence under Section 23(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987. The courts imposed total fines of RM14,000.
Noraini was speaking at a press conference after an RTD operation around the Padang Besar Roundabout yesterday.
She said the department took the matter seriously as unlicensed passenger transport services violated the law and left passengers without insurance protection in the event of an accident.
On a separate issue, Noraini said the department had stepped up enforcement against drivers and vehicles registered in Thailand operating in Perlis.

5468aa8cec101f3b: MANILA: US authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors," secretary of state Marco Rubio said Wednesday.

The top American diplomat's comments, on the sidelines of a Southeast Asian summit, follow multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to a Microsoft email and messaging breakdown, banking and mobile pay problems and the outage of a top-secret US government communications network.

"The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever - we have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other," Rubio told reporters in Manila while on a trip to Asia with US president Donald Trump.
